```{python}
import json
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import plotly.express as px
import polars as pl
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import display

comparison = json.loads(Path("comparison.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
runs = comparison["runs"]


def show_table(frame):
    table = GT(frame)
    strings = [name for name, dtype in frame.schema.items() if dtype == pl.String]
    numbers = [name for name, dtype in frame.schema.items() if dtype.is_float()]
    if strings:
        table = table.fmt(escape, columns=strings)
    if numbers:
        table = table.fmt_number(columns=numbers, decimals=4)
    costs = [name for name in ("USD total", "Known USD") if name in frame.columns]
    if costs:
        table = table.fmt_number(columns=costs, decimals=6)
    display(table)


show_table(pl.DataFrame({"Comparison": [comparison["title"]]}))
```

This report reads saved predictions and makes no provider calls. It compares the
same selected source records across runs. It does not select prompts or routing
thresholds, or establish statistical significance. Mock runs test the pipeline.

## Data compatibility

```{python}
print(f"Selected records per run: {runs[0]['metrics']['support']}")
print(f"Selected dataset SHA256: {comparison['dataset_sha256']}")
if comparison["historical_inputs_verified"]:
    print("Historical inputs verified: current selected data match every run's saved fingerprint.")
else:
    print("Historical inputs unverified for legacy runs:")
    for warning in comparison["warnings"]:
        print(warning)
if runs[0]["metrics"]["support"] < 30:
    print("Small smoke sample: use these results to check the pipeline, not to rank model quality.")
```

## Overall comparison

Accuracy and macro F1 include unresolved predictions in their denominators.
Coverage is the fraction with a resolved prediction. Latency reflects recorded
provider requests, including the original timing when predictions came from cache;
it is not the elapsed time of generating this report.

```{python}
summary = pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"], "Provider": run["provider"], "Model": run["model"],
        "Simulated": run["simulated"], "Records": run["metrics"]["support"],
        "Accuracy": run["metrics"]["accuracy"],
        "Macro F1": run["metrics"]["macro_f1"],
        "Coverage": run["metrics"]["operational_coverage"],
        "P50 ms": run["metrics"]["latency_p50_ms"],
        "P95 ms": run["metrics"]["latency_p95_ms"],
        "USD total": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_total"],
        "USD per 1,000": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_per_1000"],
        "Priced fraction": run["metrics"]["cost_priced_fraction"],
    }
    for run in runs
], schema_overrides={"USD total": pl.Float64, "USD per 1,000": pl.Float64})
show_table(summary.select("Run", "Provider", "Model", "Records", "Accuracy", "Macro F1", "Coverage"))
```

## Latency and cost

```{python}
show_table(summary.select("Run", "P50 ms", "P95 ms", "USD total", "USD per 1,000", "Priced fraction"))
```

Costs are token-based USD estimates, not billing statements or additional spend
from this comparison. A null total means pricing is incomplete; it does not mean
zero cost. The plots below exclude runs with an incomplete cost estimate.

## Quality versus cost and latency

```{python}
priced = summary.filter(pl.col("USD per 1,000").is_not_null())
if priced.height:
    fig = px.scatter(
        priced, x="USD per 1,000", y="Macro F1", color="Run",
        hover_data=["Provider", "Model", "Accuracy", "Coverage", "Records"],
        title="Macro F1 versus estimated cost",
    )
    fig.update_traces(marker_size=14)
    fig.show(renderer="notebook")
else:
    print("Cost plot unavailable: no completely priced runs.")

fig = px.scatter(
    summary, x="P50 ms", y="Macro F1", color="Run",
    hover_data=["Provider", "Model", "Accuracy", "Coverage", "P95 ms", "Records"],
    title="Macro F1 versus median request latency",
)
fig.update_traces(marker_size=14)
fig.show(renderer="notebook")
```

## Language results

```{python}
languages = pl.DataFrame([
    {"Run": run["label"], "Language": language, **values}
    for run in runs
    for language, values in run["metrics"]["by_language"].items()
])
show_table(languages)
```

## Prediction disagreements

Only records where the runs predict different labels are shown. `unresolved`
means a provider failed to return a label. Agreement can include shared mistakes;
it is not a substitute for comparing against reference labels.

```{python}
if comparison["disagreements"]:
    show_table(pl.DataFrame(comparison["disagreements"]))
else:
    print("No prediction disagreements on these records.")
```

## Usage and provenance

```{python}
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"],
        "Input tokens": run["metrics"]["usage_input_tokens_total"],
        "Output tokens": run["metrics"]["usage_output_tokens_total"],
        "Usage fraction": run["metrics"]["usage_records_fraction"],
        "Known USD": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_known_total"],
    }
    for run in runs
]))
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"], "Source folder": run["path"],
        "Prompt": run["prompt_version"],
        "Simulated": run["simulated"],
        "Historical input verified": run["historical_input_verified"],
    }
    for run in runs
]))
```

Token totals sum known usage; missing usage does not imply a free request. These
results use synthetic financial feedback with template variations. Exact
matching does not establish independence or real-world generalization.
